titleZh: 酒店客用品库存积压，采购量该怎么调整？
titleEn: Hotel Guest Supply Overstock: How Should Purchasing Quantities Be Adjusted?
summaryZh: 酒店客用品库存积压，应先核清库房、楼层存量和在途订单，再结合实际消耗与交货周期调整采购量。用一张采购量核对表，同时检查库存占用、缺货与紧急采购。
summaryEn: Reconcile central and floor stock, outstanding orders, consumption and delivery dates before changing hotel guest supply purchases. An item-level checklist helps review excess stock, shortages and emergency orders.
contentZh:
酒店客用品库存积压，采购量该怎么调整？

酒店客用品库存积压时，应先盘清库房、楼层和在途订单，再按实际消耗与到货时间调整单品采购量。统一削减采购预算，可能留下用不掉的物料，却让常用品先断货。

采购申请看的是“还要买多少”，库房看的是“账上还有多少”，客房部关心的是“今天能不能拿到”。如果三方使用的数量和时间口径不同，同一家酒店就可能一边积压，一边紧急补货。总经理要先让这几笔数对上，再决定哪些停订、哪些少订、哪些仍需补足。

先把客用品库存分清楚

盘点应从具体单品开始。名称相近、包装不同、适用房型不同的用品，不能仅凭“都是牙具”或“都是拖鞋”合并计算。采购按箱、库房按包、楼层按件记录时，先统一换算单位，否则订货量算得再细也没有意义。

同一单品至少要看三个位置：中央库房、楼层备品间与工作车、已经下单但尚未到货的订单。楼层已有的合格备品仍是酒店存量，从库房发到楼层只是内部转移，不能在全店口径中直接当成客人已经消耗。

账面有货，也不代表能够使用。破损、受潮、过期、待验收或因品牌更换不再适用的用品，应单独列出；已为确定活动或特定房型留用的数量，要说明用途。预留需求若已计入预计消耗，就不要再从可用库存重复扣减。

Oracle的酒店物资管理资料将现存量、订货建议、实际与计划用量比较列为不同管理对象。这支持一个基本做法：采购审批要同时看存量和消耗，不能只看上一次买了多少。该资料不提供适用于所有酒店的库存天数，也不能证明某家酒店已经采购过量。

怎样看清实际消耗

如果楼层每月从库房领出一批用品，却始终留下不少余量，直接把领用量作为下月采购依据，就会将楼层存货继续叠加。

可以先选一种记录较完整的常用客用品，由客房部与库管在同一时点盘点。核对期初存量、期间收货、期末存量，以及退货、报废和其他非客用去向。先找出实物减少量，再解释其中多少用于客人、多少属于损耗；不能把无法解释的盘亏全部归入正常客耗。

对下一阶段需求的估计，还要与物品使用方式对应。按人使用的用品要考虑预计入住人数，按房补充的用品要看实际使用规则；长住、连住与退房清洁的补充方式可能不同。统一用“出租房晚乘一个定额”，容易把客群和补充规则的差异抹掉。

没有可靠消耗记录时，不宜直接大幅压低存量。先在一组常用品上建立盘点与去向记录，保留有依据的缓冲，再修正采购量。用品质量、卫生要求和已经承诺的服务标准，不随库存目标一起下调。

酒店客用品采购，要同时算数量和到货日

每次订货，先明确这批货要覆盖到什么时候。如果每周审核一次采购，而供应商从确认订单到验收入库还需要若干天，那么覆盖范围应考虑审核间隔与实际交货时间，不能只算下一次采购会之前的消耗。

一个可用的计算起点是：覆盖期内预计消耗，加上有依据的缓冲量，减去当前可用存量，再减去覆盖期内确认可到货的在途量，得到建议新增采购量。结果小于零时，先不新增；已有订单能否改期、减量或分批交付，还须核对双方约定。

但总量算够了，并不等于每天都有货。应再沿日期检查：当前库存能撑到哪一天，第一批在途货何时能够验收入库。到货前已经出现缺口的订单，不能拿来抵扣眼前的补货需要。供应商尚未确认交期的数量，也不应与可按时到货的数量等同处理。

下面仅作计算示例，不是行业定额。某单品覆盖期内预计用量为900件，另留150件缓冲，中央库房与楼层合计可用400件，已有300件确认能在需要前到货。建议新增量为350件。若那300件要到关键使用日之后才能到货，就要先处理前段缺口，不能仍按350件照常下单。新增订单也有交期；来不及补上的缺口，应优先核查店内调拨或与供应商协商加急的可行性，并同步调整后续订单，避免应急补货又变成新的积压。

实际下单还要检查整箱规格、最低起订量和储存条件。为了凑折扣买进大批存货，可能增加占用、过期或换版风险；若供应商只接受大批量订单，可以比较分批交付是否可行。账面单价更低，不自动说明这次采购更合算。

把采购量核对表带进审批

不必先更换系统。一张按单品填写的核对表，就能让采购、客房和财务围绕同一批数据讨论。每个单品记录以下内容。

品项与口径：名称、规格、使用场景和统一计量单位，注明每箱换算数量。

可用存量：中央库房、楼层及工作车的实盘数；另列不可用数量和原因，注明盘点日期。

在途订单：未交数量、供应商确认到货日、验收所需时间，以及是否允许调整交付。

需求依据：覆盖起止日、预计入住或使用量、相应消耗规则，以及缓冲量的理由。波动较大的交期和需求要单独说明。

采购判断：建议新增量、按日核查发现的缺口、起订与整箱限制，以及停订、减量、正常补货或协商分批交付的选择。

复核结果：实际到货与消耗、期末剩余、缺货和紧急采购记录，用于下一轮修正。

客房负责人确认楼层存量与使用需求，采购负责人确认在途订单和供货条件，库管核对实盘与收货，财务复核数量、金额及口径。跨部门调拨、改变交付条件或突破既定采购权限的事项，再由相应授权人决定。签字的作用是确认这些依据，而不是用多一道审批代替核对。

先试调一组常用品

选择规格稳定、记录较清楚的一组用品，从下一次下单开始试调，至少观察一个完整的订货、到货与消耗周期。试验范围要小到能够查清每次异常，也要覆盖真实供货过程，不能只观察采购付款减少的那几天。

复盘同时看三类结果：积压存量是否减少，缺货与紧急采购是否增加，实际消耗与预计消耗的差距能否解释。还应区分付款变化与用品消耗变化。少买一批货可以暂时减少付款，但如果消耗没有改变，就不能把同一金额直接写成经营成本节省。

若供应商开始延迟交货，入住需求明显变化，或某项服务因缺货受到影响，应先恢复必要供应，再调整缓冲和下单时间。长交期、定制包装、品牌指定采购以及需求强季节性的酒店，尤其不能照搬短交期常用品的库存安排。

酒店客用品补货的目标，是在需要的时候有合格用品可用，同时减少没有用途的占用。下一张采购单送来时，先选一组常用品，把“店里还有多少、已经订了多少、何时真正需要”核清，再批准数量。
contentEn:
Hotel Guest Supply Overstock: How Should Purchasing Quantities Be Adjusted?

When hotel guest supplies accumulate, first reconcile stock in the central store, on guestroom floors and on outstanding orders. Adjust quantities for each item using actual consumption and delivery dates. An across-the-board budget cut may leave unwanted stock in place while essential items run out.

Purchasing asks how much to buy, the store looks at recorded balances, and housekeeping needs supplies available today. Different quantity definitions and time periods can produce both overstock and urgent purchases. The general manager should reconcile these figures before deciding what to stop, reduce or replenish.

Clarify the guest supply inventory

Start with individual items. Similar names do not make different packaging or supplies intended for different room types interchangeable. If purchasing records cartons, the store packs and floors individual pieces, agree the conversion first.

Review three locations: the central store, floor pantries and housekeeping carts, and orders placed but not yet received. Serviceable supplies on floors remain hotel inventory. Moving them out of the central store is an internal transfer and does not establish guest consumption across the property.

Recorded stock may be unusable. Separate damaged, damp, expired, uninspected or obsolete branded items. Explain quantities reserved for confirmed events or specific room types. If reserved demand is already included in forecast consumption, do not also deduct it from available stock.

Oracle's hotel materials management documentation treats stock on hand, order proposals and comparisons of actual and planned usage as distinct management objects. This supports reviewing both stock and consumption when approving purchases. The documentation provides neither a universal stockholding period nor evidence that a particular hotel has overpurchased.

Establish actual consumption

If floors regularly retain some of their monthly issues, using those issues as the next month's purchasing basis can keep adding floor stock.

Select a frequently used item with reasonably complete records. Housekeeping and the storekeeper should count at the same point in time. Reconcile opening stock, receipts, closing stock, returns, write-offs and other uses unrelated to guests. Establish the physical reduction, then explain how much was guest use and how much was loss. Unexplained discrepancies should not all be classified as normal guest consumption.

Forecast demand according to how the item is used. Supplies issued per person require expected guest numbers; supplies replenished per room require the actual replenishment rules. Extended stays, stayovers and departure cleaning may involve different practices. Multiplying occupied room nights by one fixed allowance can conceal these differences.

Where consumption records are unreliable, avoid an immediate large stock reduction. Build count and usage records for a small group of common items, retain a justified buffer and then revise purchasing quantities. Quality, hygiene requirements and promised service standards remain part of the decision.

Calculate quantities alongside delivery dates

Define the period each order must cover. If purchases are reviewed weekly and the supplier needs additional days from confirmation to accepted receipt, the coverage period should consider both the review interval and actual lead time. It should extend beyond the next purchasing meeting where necessary.

A useful starting calculation is forecast consumption during the coverage period plus a justified buffer, less current usable stock and outstanding quantities confirmed to arrive within that period. This gives the proposed additional purchase. If the result is negative, do not add an order yet. Check agreed terms before reducing, rescheduling or splitting an existing order.

An adequate total does not guarantee availability every day. Check when current stock will run out and when the first outstanding delivery will be accepted into inventory. A delivery arriving after a shortage begins cannot cover the earlier gap. Unconfirmed delivery dates should not be treated as reliable supply.

The following is a calculation example, not an industry allowance. Forecast consumption is 900 pieces, the buffer is 150, usable central and floor stock totals 400, and 300 pieces are confirmed to arrive before they are needed. The proposed additional purchase is 350 pieces. If the 300 arrive after the critical usage date, address the earlier gap before proceeding with that quantity. New orders also have lead times. Where they cannot arrive soon enough, check internal transfers or discuss expedited delivery with the supplier, then adjust later orders so that emergency purchases do not create fresh overstock.

Check carton sizes, minimum orders and storage conditions before placing the order. Buying heavily for a discount may increase stockholding, expiry or packaging-obsolescence risks. If a supplier requires a large order, consider whether staged deliveries are feasible. A lower unit price alone does not establish a better purchase.

Bring a purchasing quantity checklist into approval

A system replacement need not be the first step. An item-level checklist can give purchasing, housekeeping and finance a shared basis for discussion. Record the following for each item.

Item and units: name, specification, use and common unit of measure, including pieces per carton.

Usable stock: physical counts in the central store, on floors and on carts; list unusable quantities and reasons separately, with the count date.

Outstanding orders: undelivered quantities, supplier-confirmed arrival dates, inspection time and whether delivery arrangements can be changed.

Demand basis: coverage dates, expected occupancy or usage, applicable consumption rules and the reason for the buffer. Explain significant variability in demand or delivery times.

Purchasing decision: proposed additional quantity, shortages identified by date, minimum-order and carton constraints, and whether to stop, reduce, replenish normally or negotiate staged delivery.

Review results: actual receipts and consumption, closing balances, shortages and urgent purchases, to inform the next review.

Housekeeping confirms floor stock and demand; purchasing confirms outstanding orders and supply conditions; the storekeeper checks physical counts and receipts; finance reviews quantities, amounts and definitions. Internal transfers, changes to delivery terms and decisions beyond purchasing authority go to the authorised decision-maker. Signatures confirm the underlying information; an extra approval step cannot perform that reconciliation.

Trial an adjustment with a small group of common items

Choose items with stable specifications and reasonably clear records. Start with the next order and observe at least one complete ordering, delivery and consumption cycle. Keep the scope small enough to explain exceptions while covering the real supply process. A few days of lower purchasing payments are insufficient.

Review whether excess stock decreases, whether shortages and emergency purchases increase, and whether differences between forecast and actual consumption can be explained. Distinguish payments from consumption. Buying less can temporarily reduce payments, but the same amount cannot be described as an operating cost saving if consumption has not changed.

If deliveries slip, demand changes materially or shortages affect service, restore necessary supply before revising buffers and order timing. Hotels with long lead times, custom packaging, mandated brand purchasing or strongly seasonal demand should adapt the approach rather than copy arrangements for common items with short lead times.

The aim of hotel guest supply replenishment is to have serviceable items available when needed while reducing stock without a use. For the next purchase request, select a small group of common items and establish what the hotel holds, what it has already ordered and when it will actually need the supplies before approving quantities.
author: 迈创兄弟C&T
